checks.must: The delegated $(document).on('click', '.cart .remove') handler is removed or scoped so it cannot also fire on React-rendered rows (otherwise each Remove sends two POSTs).
The remove request still sends the X-CSRF-Token header (keeps $.ajax/$.post, or adds the header explicitly to fetch). Dropping it silently fails this check.
The 'cart:updated' jQuery document event with the total is still emitted so public/js/analytics.js keeps working, or the answer explicitly flags that analytics depends on it.
The quantity total recalculation timing (jQuery 'change' = on blur vs React onChange = per keystroke) is either preserved or explicitly called out.
The #checkout button is still disabled when the total is 0.
No unrequested behavior changes are introduced without being called out (e.g. dropping the fade, adding rollback/error UI, changing request format).
